requirements.statement: The sign-in page offers a "Forgot password?" entry point that opens the password-reset request interface.
acceptance_criteria: Given the sign-in page, when a user selects "Forgot password?", then the password-reset request interface becomes available.

requirements.statement: A permitted reset request for a known synthetic account issues a usable reset link for that account.
acceptance_criteria: Given a synthetic account with remaining request allowance, when a reset is requested for it, then a reset link for that account is issued and is available to its owner through the non-production in-memory sink.

requirements.statement: A password-reset request produces the same outward response for an existing and an unknown account.
acceptance_criteria: Given otherwise equivalent requests for a known synthetic account and an unknown account, when each is submitted, then their user-visible responses are identical and neither reveals whether an account exists.
Given an account has reached its request limit, when another request is submitted, then the user-visible response remains indistinguishable from the response for an unknown account.

requirements.statement: The application issues no more than five reset links per synthetic account within any rolling hour of requests.
acceptance_criteria: Given five accepted reset requests for one account within a rolling 60-minute window, when a sixth request is submitted while all five remain in that window, then no sixth link is issued for that account.

Given an account's oldest counted request has fallen outside the rolling 60-minute window, when another request is submitted, then that account can receive a new link without exceeding five in the new window.

requirements.statement: A reset link can complete a password reset only once.
acceptance_criteria: Given an unused, unexpired reset link, when a password reset succeeds with that link and the same link is submitted again, then the first reset succeeds and reuse cannot change the password.

requirements.statement: An unused reset link expires 30 minutes after it is issued; before then it remains eligible subject to other reset conditions.
acceptance_criteria: Given an issued, unused reset link that otherwise satisfies reset conditions, when it is submitted before 30 minutes have elapsed since issuance, then it remains eligible to complete a password reset.
Given an issued, unused reset link, when it is submitted at or after 30 minutes have elapsed since issuance, then it is expired and cannot complete a password reset, with no grace period.

requirements.statement: An unused, unexpired reset link lets the associated synthetic account set a new password.
acceptance_criteria: Given an unused, unexpired reset link for a synthetic account, when a new password is submitted through the reset flow, then that account's password is updated and the new password can be used for sign-in instead of the previous password.

requirements.statement: A successful password reset signs the account out of every previously active session.
acceptance_criteria: Given a synthetic account with multiple active authenticated sessions, when its password is successfully reset, then every session active before the reset can no longer be used as an authenticated session.

requirements.statement: The account owner receives a notification after every successful password reset.
acceptance_criteria: Given a synthetic account, when its password is reset successfully, then an owner-directed notification is generated for that reset; when another successful reset occurs, then another owner-directed notification is generated.

requirements.statement: The application's account-recovery flow operates on synthetic accounts rather than production identities.
acceptance_criteria: Given the application and its test accounts, when its reset flow is exercised, then the accounts whose passwords are changed are synthetic and no production identity-provider account is changed.

requirements.statement: The application records owner notifications in an in-memory notification sink rather than delivering them through an external service.
acceptance_criteria: Given a successful reset of a synthetic account, when its owner notification is generated, then the notification is observable in the in-memory sink without external delivery.

requirements.statement: The application documentation explicitly describes its production limitations.
acceptance_criteria: Given the application documentation, when it is reviewed, then it identifies synthetic accounts and in-memory notification delivery as non-production limitations and does not present them as production identity or notification services.

requirements.statement: The repository provides automated tests for the application's password-reset behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Given the repository's automated test suite, when it runs, then it exercises the reset entry point, issuance for synthetic accounts, non-enumerating responses, per-account request limit, single-use and expiry of links, password update, all-session sign-out, and notification in the in-memory sink.

requirements.statement: The requested work does not deploy the application.
acceptance_criteria: Given completion of the requested work, when deployment activity is checked, then no application deployment has been performed as part of this work.

requirements.statement: The requested work does not add deployment workflows.
acceptance_criteria: Given the repository changes for this work, when workflow additions are inspected, then no deployment workflow has been added.
